title: @font-face and font loading strategy
learningObjectives: Explain @font-face and font loading strategy and implement a maintainable CSS workflow or lab.

understand.concept: @font-face defines a downloadable or locally available font family, source, weight, style, and related descriptors. Font loading strategy includes choosing suitable formats, limiting weights and subsets, setting font-display, and providing fallback families.
understand.whyItMatters: Fonts affect performance, layout stability, licensing, privacy, and language glyph coverage. Test all required scripts and avoid loading font files that the page does not use.
understand.analogy: A web font is a resource the page can request; the design should still be readable while it arrives or if it fails.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the design; implementation must follow browser APIs, CSS behaviour, and accessibility requirements.

explain.narrative: This example uses a local source for demonstration. A production declaration should reference a properly licensed font file and include suitable fallback families.

examples.explanation: This example uses a local source for demonstration. A production declaration should reference a properly licensed font file and include suitable fallback families.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered demonstration of the workflow or interactive lab starter.

practise.guidedTask: Define a font face with a fallback stack and font-display. Document the weights and character subsets actually needed for your languages.
practise.independentTask: Build a small production-minded example. Validate input, keep the baseline usable, and document browser and accessibility checks.
hints: Keep one canonical state for synchronized controls.
Use textContent for user-generated output rather than unsafe HTML insertion.
Test keyboard operation and invalid input.
